title: The 21-record 2026-09-14 datemodified batch that sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's 2026-09-18 review found frozen for three nights has resumed -- in lockstep, in the same fixed relative order, twice -- arguing the freeze was a pause in a shared feed-regeneration job, not the per-record stop gdacs-fl-1103815 shows
statement: sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's 2026-09-18 review (foreknown/proposals/sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json, review.history[2]) found 17 OPEN GDACS futures whose properties.datemodified all landed within about eight seconds of each other in the 2026-09-15 snapshot (2026-09-14T20:25:15 through :23) and had stayed frozen there through 2026-09-17, and it left open, as a watch_for, whether any of them would individually resume echoing. Re-scanning foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-12/gdacs.json through foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-19/gdacs.json for every future whose datemodified fell in that same 2026-09-14T20:25:15-23 window finds 21 such futures (gdacs-dr-1017863, gdacs-eq-1544720, gdacs-eq-1546617, gdacs-eq-1548377, gdacs-eq-1548473, gdacs-eq-1554552, gdacs-eq-1557236, gdacs-eq-1558059, gdacs-fl-1104124, gdacs-tc-1001270, gdacs-tc-1001279, gdacs-wf-1029260, gdacs-wf-1029331, gdacs-wf-1029540, gdacs-wf-1029628, gdacs-wf-1029643, gdacs-wf-1029649, gdacs-wf-1029794, gdacs-wf-1029958, gdacs-wf-1030252, gdacs-wf-1030534; 19 of these are OPEN with zero REVISED events in foreknown/registry.json, matching the review's class, and two -- gdacs-fl-1104124 and gdacs-wf-1030252 -- carry exactly one REVISED event each, which is why this scan's count (21) differs from the review's (17)). None of the 21 stayed frozen: every one advanced on the night of 2026-09-18 (values clustering 2026-09-18T10:00:43 through :15, a 32-second spread) and again on 2026-09-19 (2026-09-19T09:40:18 through :25, a 7-second spread) -- the freeze the review characterised as possibly a stop was a three-night pause, not a stop. The decisive detail is the order: sorting each night's 21 timestamps puts gdacs-fl-1104124 first and gdacs-tc-1001270 last on 2026-09-15 (the frozen value), on 2026-09-18, and on 2026-09-19, with the same relative ordering of every record in between on all three nights. Extending the check to gdacs-fl-1104124 alone back through 2026-08-28 (its first appearance in the registry) across the 21 nights it has been preserved shows two earlier, shorter freezes of the same shape (2026-08-29 to 2026-08-30, 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-01, each two nights) before the three-night 2026-09-15-17 one, and on every night it does change, the value clusters with the group's other members, never alone -- this is not a single anomalous pause, it is the batch's ordinary cadence, of which 2026-09-15 through 2026-09-17 is the third and longest gap so far. A fixed relative order, repeated verbatim across a pause and two resumptions and a run of prior nights, is consistent with a source-side job that iterates a stable list and re-stamps datemodified on each pass regardless of content, and is not consistent with 21 independent records happening to be re-examined by GDACS staff in the identical sequence three times running.
method: Loaded foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-15/gdacs.json and extracted every feature whose properties.datemodified falls in [2026-09-14T20:25:15, 2026-09-14T20:25:23.999999] (21 features). Cross-checked each against foreknown/registry.json to confirm existence, hazard-type-derived future id, OPEN status, and REVISED-event count (19 at zero, 2 at one). Loaded the same 21 eventids' properties.datemodified from foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-12/gdacs.json through foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-19/gdacs.json, tabulated per-night values, and confirmed all 21 held the 2026-09-15 value unchanged through 2026-09-17 (three-night freeze) and all 21 changed together on 2026-09-18 and again on 2026-09-19. Sorted each of the three clustered nights (2026-09-15 frozen value, 2026-09-18, 2026-09-19) by timestamp and confirmed identical relative ordering of all 21 records across all three sorts. Extended a per-night datemodified trace for gdacs-fl-1104124 alone from its first appearance (foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-28/gdacs.json) through 2026-09-19 (21 nights preserved, 16 changed from the prior night, 4 unchanged) to check whether the 2026-09-15-17 freeze was anomalous or part of a recurring cadence, finding two earlier two-night freezes (2026-08-29 to 2026-08-30, 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-01) and a change value clustered with the group's other members on every night it did move. Read sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's full review history to confirm this batch matches its 2026-09-18 review's population and open watch_for rather than describing a new class. No code changed; python -m pip install -e ./practice, python -m pytest practice/tests (185 passed, unchanged from obs-2026-09-19-1.json), python stage/generate.py --repo-root . and python verify.py --repo-root . run after appending this observation and the sensor review update; all green.
worth_watching_because: This directly answers the open watch_for in sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's 2026-09-18 review by ruling out the branch it treated as live (an individual record breaking from the group the way gdacs-fl-1103815 did) and confirming the other: the whole group moves together, in the same order, or not at all. That strengthens the sensor's own falsification concern -- that datemodified reflects a source-side batch job's iteration order for at least this class of record, not per-record attention -- with evidence now spanning a pause and two independent resumptions rather than a single historical snapshot. It also means gdacs-fl-1103815's now-17-night-frozen datemodified is a materially different kind of signal than these 21 records' three-night pause: one is a record the batch has stopped touching at all, the other is a record the batch touches on most nights and occasionally skips for a few nights running. A promotable test_rule for this sensor needs to tell those two shapes apart, which this observation gives sharper evidence for but does not itself design.
left_alone: Not proposing a redesigned test_rule for sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json: the open design problem (separating a shared-batch touch, now confirmed periodic with multiple pause/resume cycles, from a genuine per-record freeze) is unchanged in kind by tonight's finding, only sharper in evidence, and the review already declines to attempt that redesign inline. Not treating gdacs-fl-1104124's other historical freezes (found while tracing back to 2026-08-28) as separate findings -- they are the same recurring cadence this observation already describes, not new instances. Not re-checking sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json or sensor-source-ref-episode-drift.json tonight beyond confirming via autonomy/log.jsonl that the 2026-09-19 foreknown-notary-run (the first to run since source_ref_episode_drift() was promoted and wired in) posted source_ref_episode_drift: 10, the same count obs-2026-09-19-1.json's hand-check found the night before wiring; also confirmed foreknown/registry.json still shows no second closure event on gdacs-tc-1001305 since its 2026-08-28 REAPPEARED. No memoryhole verdicts: foreknown/registry.json's newest sibling record, memoryhole/readings/2026-09-18.json (the newest reading), carries zero rule-layer abstentions across all 62 entries. darkocean's dma sub-source outage continues unchanged in shape (autonomy/log.jsonl, 2026-09-19T09:00:51+00:00, "dma": "outage: URLError"); already covered by obs-2026-08-13-2.json and obs-2026-08-22-1.json, not re-reported.
